turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good afternoon, this is Oliver calling from Acme Life Cover. I'm returning a call-back request about our life cover. Am I speaking with Sophie?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, that's me. I filled in the little form after seeing your advert in the paper. I wasn't sure anyone would actually ring.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Well, here I am! Before we go any further, could I just take your full name and date of birth, please?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Sophie Margaret Clarke, and it's the 14th of March, 1959.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Lovely, thank you, Mrs Clarke, that matches what we have. So, can I ask what got you thinking about life cover?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I've just retired, I taught primary for thirty-odd years, and I've got three grandchildren now. My pension covers me fine, but I'd like to leave them a little something. Help with university, or a deposit on a flat one day.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's a lovely reason. Do you have any existing life insurance, perhaps through your teaching pension or an old mortgage policy?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: There was something with the mortgage, but that ended when we paid it off. The teachers' pension has a death benefit, but I think that mostly goes to my husband, Graham.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Understood. And roughly what sort of sum did you have in mind for the grandchildren?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I honestly don't know. Ten thousand each, perhaps? So thirty thousand? Is that silly?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Not at all. Our cover starts at twenty-five thousand pounds and goes up to five hundred thousand, so thirty thousand sits comfortably within that. I'll explain how it works. There's no medical exam. Instead I'd ask you a few health questions, and acceptance depends on your answers.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No medical? That sounds almost too easy. What's the catch?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Fair question. The main thing to know is that for the first twelve months, the policy only pays out for accidental death. So if you passed away from an illness in that first year, it wouldn't pay out. After twelve months you're covered as normal.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I see. So if I took it out and then, heaven forbid, something happened in the first year, the grandchildren would get nothing unless it was an accident.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's right, yes. It's important you're comfortable with that.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: And the price? My friend had one where the payments kept going up every year, and she ended up cancelling it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: With ours, the premium is fixed for the whole length of the policy. Whatever you're quoted at the start is what you pay throughout. It won't creep up as you get older.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Well, that's better than hers, anyway. How much would it be?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That depends on the health questions, so shall we run through those? There are only a few.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Go on then.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Have you smoked or used any nicotine products in the last twelve months?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, never smoked.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: In the last five years, have you been diagnosed with or treated for cancer, heart disease, stroke or diabetes?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No. I take a tablet for my blood pressure, but that's all. Does that count?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Well-controlled blood pressure on its own doesn't affect acceptance for this policy. And are you currently waiting on any tests or hospital referrals?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thank you. Based on that, for thirty thousand pounds of cover, your premium would be thirty-eight pounds forty a month, fixed for the life of the policy.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Thirty-eight pounds a month. Hmm. That's more than I expected, to be honest. Over ten or fifteen years, that adds up.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: It does, and that's worth thinking about carefully. Some people compare the total they'd pay against simply saving that money for the grandchildren. The difference is the cover pays the full amount from day one for accidents, and after the first year for any cause.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, I suppose so. I'd want to talk to Graham first. We do these things together, and he might say we'd be better putting it into the children's savings accounts.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That makes complete sense. It's a big decision, and there's no rush at all. The quote is based on your answers today, so if you ring back, we'd just recheck the details.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: And if we did go ahead and then changed our minds?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: There's a thirty-day cooling-off period. If you cancel within thirty days, you get a full refund of anything you've paid.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: That's reassuring. But I'd still rather not sign up for something and then cancel it. I'll have a proper think.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Of course. Would it help if I emailed a summary of what we've discussed, including the cover amount, the monthly price and the twelve-month accidental-death-only point, so you and Graham can look at it together?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, that would be helpful. Is it the email from the form?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Yes, the one ending in btinternet dot com. I'll send that over this afternoon. You can call us back whenever suits you, or not at all if you decide it's not for you.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Thank you, Oliver. You've been very clear, I appreciate that.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: My pleasure, Mrs Clarke. Enjoy your retirement, and I hope the grandchildren appreciate their thoughtful nan. Goodbye.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Ha, we'll see! Goodbye.
